patternsToSteal.pattern: One persistent 3D world behind ordinary HTML (not a 3D site with HTML on top). Lusion's site is regular HTML flex/grid blocks with a full-screen canvas behind them; a screen-to-world projection lines 3D objects up with DOM elements, so copy stays selectable, SEO-able and reflowable while the scene 'reacts' to each section.
patternsToSteal.seenAt: https://mark-n.co/projects/lusion-reverse-engineered/ ; https://schoolofmotion.com/blog/10-websites-with-great-animation-in-2026 (Lusion: scene morphs as you scroll, revealing project info)
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Keep scene.js city as the single canvas, but register DOM 'anchors' (data-scene-anchor on each chapter) and let city.js aim the camera/light at a building that stands for that chapter (Oplossingen = the shop street, Lab = the observatory tower, Werkwijze = the pipeline bridge). The HTML stays a normal static page; the city becomes the illustration layer for every section instead of a hero-only intro. Lite mode swaps the canvas for a static poster and keeps all anchors as plain sections.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Scroll position drives the camera through a continuous scene, with the camera path pre-visualised as grey mock-ups before any shading. Igloo Inc (Awwwards Site of the Year 2024, by abeto) is one continuous WebGL canvas where scroll directly sets camera and object states; the team previs'd the camera path untextured first, then dressed it.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Define a 6-7 keyframe camera path over the night city (arrival from the stars -> street level -> a bakery facade -> the Simulatieruimte 'control room' -> the pipeline -> contact). Scroll is NOT hijacked: native scroll continues to drive the HTML; the camera just lerps toward the keyframe of the section in view. Work package: ship the path first as a greybox (flat materials, no bloom) so cloud agents can verify it headlessly with Playwright screenshots at fixed scroll offsets, then add lighting.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Make the product playable on the homepage, not described. Messenger (abeto, Awwwards Developer Site of the Year 2025) IS the product: a small-planet delivery game you play immediately. Bruno Simon's portfolio is navigated by driving a car to signposts. Framer's homepage shows its own canvas with a live agent prompt ('add a 3D image ticker') and the reply.
patternsToSteal.seenAt: https://www.awwwards.com/sites/messenger ; https://www.awwwards.com/sites/brunos-portfolio ; https://www.framer.com/ (homepage canvas preview, Design Pages Sept 2025: https://framer.com/updates/design-pages)
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: The Simulatieruimte (sim.js) is already the 'playable product'. Promote a cut-down, 20-second version of it into the first viewport: visitor picks a business type (bakker, kapper, garage...), a fictional graph appears, the agent writes 2 lines of advice, all client-side from sim-data.js and labelled 'gesimuleerd, fictieve data'. Same for the pipeline: a 'wat zou Snymis zien' replay that shows a scouted (fictional) business, a generated example page, and the approval step with a visible 'wacht op goedkeuring van Snymis' state. No fake sent state.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Switchable real-time 'rooms' instead of pages, each with a big central screen. Active Theory v4/v5: the whole site is a set of environments (neo-Tokyo alley, Venice Beach, Amsterdam canals) you switch between; work plays on translucent screens inside the scene; filters in the work section serve clients while the scenes serve creatives. They explicitly design for two audiences.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: STS has exactly the two audiences: local business owners (need clarity, trust, Dutch, no jargon) and tech-curious people/partners (want to see the AI research). Build two 'rooms' in the same city: 'De Straat' (what we do for your zaak: websites, tools, zichtbaarheid, with the 4 demo shopfronts as walk-up facades) and 'Het Lab' (Simulatieruimte, Radar, Kawa/sts-world/webshot marked prototype/in onderzoek). The nav shrinks to: Straat | Lab | Contact, plus the legal pages in the footer.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Hidden, discoverable interactions that reward curiosity without blocking the path: click-and-hold, cursor-reactive light, device tilt on mobile. Active Theory v4 uses click-and-hold and scroll as hidden layers; Lusion uses a cursor-following point light and accelerometer tilt on mobile; Unseen's menu text shimmers and the view parallaxes with the pointer.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Cheap wins for a weak GPU: one point light following the cursor over the city (uniform update, no re-render cost), 'hold to light up the street' on the hero (press-and-hold turns on every shop sign in sequence, which is literally the pitch: we make local zaken visible), and deviceorientation tilt on phones with a static fallback. All gated behind the existing lite flag and prefers-reduced-motion.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Ten-second clarity through one sentence plus the thing itself. Resend: dark page, one headline, a tactile 3D cube (Spline) that exists to make an abstract infrastructure product feel concrete; the team even 3D-printed it for early customers. Linear: monochrome, one headline, the product in device frames, minimal chrome. Raycast: 'Your shortcut to everything' with an animated launcher in the hero and one red accent used almost exclusively in a diagonal stripe.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: The H1 'Jouw zaak, zichtbaar tot in de sterren' is good but says nothing about what STS does. Steal the Resend formula: headline that names the business ('Digitale diensten en AI-tools voor lokale zaken in Antwerpen en Vlaanderen'), a one-line sub ('Websites, gratis tools en simulaties. Eerst een voorbeeld, dan pas een gesprek.'), and ONE concrete object in the hero: the city with the visitor's own sector lit up. Copy Raycast's discipline with #36E8FF: one stripe/one glow, never body text. Monochrome everything else like Linear so the accent still reads.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Deliberately deterministic, non-framework motion with a budget: Obys built their site with no client-side framework, animations on requestAnimationFrame plus Web Animations API, virtual scroll written in TypeScript; their Design Books site only fully loads pages near the top of the stack and keeps deeper ones simplified until you approach them.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Matches the no-CDN, static, <500-line-module constraint. Apply the 'load near, simplify far' rule to the city: only the district in view gets emissive signs + bloom; districts two chapters away render as flat silhouettes. Also adopt Obys's 'typography first' stance: Panchang + Switzer are already distinctive, let type carry the brand and cut decorative UI chrome.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Physics-flavoured, touchable hero objects instead of decoration: Vercel Ship 2025 used a liquid ray-marched WebGL hero plus 'badge physics' (your conference badge you can toss around); Ship 2024 had the logo dissolve into particles that drift toward the cursor (Regl). Lando Norris (Awwwards Site of the Year 2025, OFF+BRAND) uses cursor-reactive blob overlays that echo the helmet livery, i.e. the effect is tied to the brand story.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Give the visitor one physical thing to hold: a 'bedrijfskaart' (a neon shop sign or a Google-preview card) they can drag/throw in the hero; it is the same object the free tools generate (QR, Google preview). Keep it a small instanced mesh with a simple spring, not a liquid shader (GPU budget). The effect must tell the story: 'we take your zaak and make it shine', not generic blobs.

patternsToSteal.pattern: The whole site as an operating system / desktop: PostHog (Sept 2025) replaced long scrolling with draggable windows, snapping, keyboard shortcuts and a bookmarks app, arguing long pages cause tab overload; Rauno Freiberg's portfolio uses a dock, interface sounds and horizontal galleries; CentralOS/TechMe templates open projects as terminal windows and accept commands like whoami. Reception for PostHog was mixed: 'jarring at first', fights native browser features.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Do not turn the whole site into a desktop (PostHog shows the cost), but steal the 'one surface, many apps' idea for the Lab: the Simulatieruimte, the three free tools and the Radar become 'apps' that open as windows over the city instead of separate pages with repeated nav. One window at a time on mobile (sheet), draggable on desktop, URL hash per app so it stays static and linkable.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Restraint as the differentiator: Malvah (Awwwards Studio of the Year 2025) starts every project by asking what can be removed; Seventeen Agency's homepage is just an interactive vertical colour tapestry where each stripe is a gateway to one project ('minimal but expressive, branding, motion and interactions do the heavy lifting').
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Current index.html has 10 sections (hero, oplossingen, lab, werkwijze, probeer, bouwen, onderzoek, demos, vragen, contact). Collapse to 4 moments: Wat we doen (Straat) / Probeer het zelf (Lab) / Hoe we werken (pipeline + Snymis keurt elk bericht goed) / Contact. Demos become facades inside Straat, FAQ moves into a drawer, 'bouwen' and 'onderzoek' merge into Lab. Less UI, more city.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Craft satire / a fictional product built with full production value to demonstrate capability: Lusion's Oryzo AI is a year-long fake launch for a cork coaster (site, founder video, Product Hunt, GitHub) used purely to show what the studio can do.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: STS already has four fictional demo businesses; treat them like Oryzo: give each a tiny 'before/after' story (a fictional bakery in Deurne with no site -> the example site -> what the owner could test), always stamped 'fictief voorbeeld'. This is the honest version of social proof when you have no reviews yet: show craft on invented clients instead of inventing testimonials.

patternsToSteal.pattern: Audio and intro loaders as a deliberate choice, upfront and skippable: Igloo and Unseen put sound controls first; OFF+BRAND's manifesto uses an intro loader with a message. Awwwards jurors still score accessibility lowest on these sites (Lando Norris: 7.00 accessibility vs 8.60 animation).
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: intro.js can stay, but make it a 1.5 s max 'stad wordt wakker' and show the H1 immediately underneath; add an explicit 'Geluid aan' toggle (default off) and a 'Rustige modus' toggle wired to the existing lite flag. Playwright test: H1 text visible within 2 s with WebGL disabled.

patternsToSteal.pattern: The founder's favourite, eatnaked.co (MDX, Awwwards Honorable Mention 3 May 2026, Three.js + React): an e-commerce food site where the 3D product sits in the page as the hero object and the category/UI is layered over it. Note it is an Honorable Mention, not SOTD, so admire the feel, not the award.
patternsToSteal.howForSTS: Use it as the visual reference for 'product in the room': a hero where the 3D object (for STS: the lit city block / shop facade) is the page, and UI floats as a thin layer. Do not copy its React/Three.js weight; STS's own Three.js with DPR 1.5 cap and instanced buildings is the lighter equivalent.

patternsToAvoid: AI-slop defaults: centred hero + badge above the H1 + three identical icon cards, purple/indigo gradients, glassmorphism, glowing blurred orbs behind the hero, colour-topped cards, bento grids with rounded everything and no dominant cell. Critics frame it as 'the model reaching for the statistical average'; cloud agents building STS will drift there unless the work packages forbid it explicitly (https://github.com/Ferousco-dev/anti-slop-design ; https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/ai-design-slop-and-how-to-spot-it ; https://dev.to/james_anderson_h/the-purple-gradient-problem-why-ai-ui-all-looks-alike-and-how-to-fix-it-3j65).

Scroll-jacking and locked scroll: keep the wheel native, make every animation interruptible, never make content visible only mid-animation; prefers-reduced-motion must get a static variant, not an invisible one (W3C TAG note). Lerp the camera toward the section in view instead of owning the scroll (https://redskystudios.co.uk/news/scroll-jacking-annoying-when-abused-delightful-when-done-right ; https://frontendchecklist.io/rules/accessibility/scrolljacking ; https://lists.w3.org/Archives/Public/public-css-archive/2022Jun/0886.html).

WebGL as decoration: Active Theory's own rule is that WebGL 'becomes noise rather than adding meaning' when it is only ornament. Every 3D element on STS must map to a claim (lit sign = zichtbaarheid, control room = Simulatieruimte, bridge = pipeline) (https://lbbonline.com/news/Craft-Matters-by-Active-Theory).

Whole-site OS/desktop metaphors and 'chat-first' homepages that remove the scannable page: PostHog's OS site was called jarring and fights browser features; Docket tested an ask-first hero and rejected it because it 'stopped feeling like a real marketing website', keeping a page with the agent layered on top. Use overlays/windows for the Lab only; never hide 'what we do' behind a prompt (https://posthog.com/blog/why-os ; https://www.docket.io/blog/designing-docket-frameless ; https://www.fortune.com/2025/08/26/homepage-is-dead-future-is-question-search-chatbots-ai).

Award-site accessibility debt: even Site of the Year 2025 scored 7.0 on accessibility vs 8.6 on animation; unskippable intros, audio autoplay, canvas-only text. STS: H1 and nav in DOM before any canvas, sound off by default, lite mode reachable in one click (https://www.awwwards.com/sites/lando-norris).

Heavy 3D without a budget: beaucoup.studio admits their 3D-configurator assets were too heavy; eatnaked-style React+Three stacks are not the model for a weak GPU. Keep DPR 1.5 cap, instanced buildings, no animated blur/box-shadow, pause rAF on visibilitychange, district-level LOD (https://beaucoup.studio/en/projects/that-original).

Fake proof borrowed from product sites: Linear/Raycast/Resend lean on logos, counters and testimonials. STS has none yet; do not imitate with placeholders. Use fictional-but-labelled demos (Oryzo model) and the real human-in-the-loop promise instead.
Pricing/'from EUR' blocks and urgency widgets common on agency templates: forbidden by the brief (every quote per client, no fake scarcity).

Generic 'full-page game' portfolios (Bruno Simon clones): usability score 7.83 and commenters call it 'just a game'; a business owner from Deurne must find 'wat kost een gesprek' without learning controls. Keep a plain path always visible (https://www.awwwards.com/sites/brunos-portfolio ; https://news.hada.io/topic?id=24963).
oneThingInterpretations: 1. De Stad als enige navigatie (Lusion/Igloo/Active Theory model): the night city is the site. Each chapter is a district with a landmark; the nav bar is replaced by a thin 'kompas' (Straat | Lab | Werkwijze | Contact) that flies the camera to the district while the HTML section scrolls into view underneath. Demos are walk-up shopfronts, tools are kiosks, the Simulatieruimte is a control tower. Lite mode: the same sections with a static city poster and the kompas as plain anchors.

2. Eén persistente console (Raycast/Linear/cmdk model): a single dark command strip pinned to the bottom (or Ctrl+K) replaces the nav, FAQ, tool launchers and contact form. Typing 'kapper' lights the hairdresser facade and loads a fictional sim; 'qr' opens the WhatsApp QR tool inline; 'contact' opens the form. Every result is a static route or a client-side action; the console also hosts Kawa later as a clearly labelled prototype. The city stays as the backdrop that reacts to console commands.

3. STS OS / het Lab-bureau (PostHog/Rauno model, scoped): the homepage keeps a short scannable page, but the Lab is one surface where Simulatieruimte, Radar, zichtbaarheidscheck, Google preview, WhatsApp QR and the three prototypes open as windows over the city (one sheet at a time on mobile, hash-routed). This literally 'removes UI' (4 pages of repeated chrome) and 'integrates it into a thing': a desk Snymis works at, with the human-approval inbox as a visible, honest window ('wacht op goedkeuring').

4. Een begeleide vlucht (Igloo/Vercel Ship model): a 60-second, scroll-driven camera flight from the stars down to one street in Antwerpen, through 5 keyframes that each state one thing we do (websites met gratis voorbeeld, gratis tools, simulaties, onderzoek, afspraak). Native scroll, camera lerps, each stop has a 'probeer dit' micro-interaction. A 'Sla de vlucht over' link and reduced-motion variant drop straight to the static chapters.

5. Een gesprek met de stad (Docket hybrid, not chat-first): the page stays, but a single conversational guide ('Wat voor zaak heb je?') sits in the hero. Three or four fixed choices (horeca, kapper, garage, bakker, aannemer, praktijk) re-light the city, swap the demo facade, pre-fill the Simulatieruimte with that sector's fictional data and tailor the 'wat we voor jou doen' copy. No LLM in the browser, no backend: a static decision tree in JS, honestly labelled; Kawa can later replace the tree as a marked prototype.

6. (bonus) Het lichtschakelaar-ritueel: the whole first screen is one gesture: press and hold to switch the street lights on, shop by shop; each sign that lights up is a service line ('website', 'Google-profiel', 'WhatsApp', 'simulatie'). Releasing leaves the city lit and the nav revealed. It is UI removed into a thing, costs almost nothing on the GPU (emissive uniform per instance), and encodes the emotional pitch: we make your zaak visible.
